plans.note: Section 7 is the express limitation-of-liability provision; check whether the cap is mutual, tied to a meaningful multiple of fees paid, and whether carve-outs (IP infringement, confidentiality, gross negligence/willful misconduct, indemnity obligations) exist. Heading pairing with 'Indemnification of Contractor' signals a vendor-favourable, one-sided construct.

Section 7 appears to contain only a Customer-side indemnity running to the Contractor; a Vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims and its own negligence/misconduct is likely absent and must be inserted, with the Clear Capital indemnity narrowed. Section 5 reps may support the IP non-infringement hook.

No covenants/restrictive-covenant section appears in the outline; scan the purpose-of-engagement and termination provisions for any incidental restriction on Clear Capital's business lines or products before concluding absence.

Check Section 1 (scope/purpose) for sole-source or 'Contractor shall be the exclusive provider' language and Section 3 for fee structures that presuppose exclusivity; otherwise likely absent and no change needed.

Pricing terms sit in Section 3 (Contractor's Compensation); confirm there is no clause requiring Clear Capital to extend best/most-favourable terms to the Contractor. Direction matters only if such an obligation runs against us.

No personnel or covenants section is listed; review termination and engagement-scope text for hire/solicit restrictions on Clear Capital, which would need a 12-month cap and a general-advertising carve-out.

Section 6 is the termination provision; verify Clear Capital has convenience termination on short notice without penalty or accelerated fees, and that any Contractor convenience right is removed or limited to non-payment/expiry.

Term/renewal mechanics would normally sit in the unlisted Section 2 or in Section 6; check for auto-renewal, notice window and uplift caps. Flag as absent only after confirming no renewal language in Section 6.

The outline shows no general/miscellaneous section, so governing law and venue appear to be missing; check the preamble and the tail of Section 7 for any embedded law/arbitration reference before proposing an insertion.

No assignment or change-of-control clause is visible; if none exists, add a provision permitting Clear Capital to assign to affiliates and successors and barring Contractor termination on our change of control. Section 6 is the natural home.

Section 4 governs ownership of materials related to the Services and acceptance; confirm all deliverables and Clear Capital data/pre-existing IP vest in us on creation (not on payment), with no assignment or broad licence back to the Contractor.

Any licence to residual Contractor tools or background IP will sit in Section 4 (with scope possibly cross-referenced to Section 1 Services); ensure it extends to affiliates and contractors and is perpetual/irrevocable for delivered work.

No audit or records clause is listed; check Section 3 for fee-verification or usage-audit rights against Clear Capital. If present, limit to once annually, prior written notice, business hours and Contractor cost.

Look in Section 3 for late-payment penalties, interest or early-termination charges and in Section 7 for any stipulated-damages language payable by Clear Capital; direction rule only bites where the amount runs against us.

Section 5 pairs Contractor warranties with a disclaimer; confirm a services/conformity-to-Specifications warranty of meaningful duration with re-performance or refund, and push back on any broad 'AS IS'/implied-warranty disclaimer. Section 4 acceptance mechanics are the related remedy hook.

No insurance section appears in the outline; expect to add standard coverages (CGL, professional liability/E&O, cyber, workers' comp) with certificates, most naturally adjacent to the Contractor reps in Section 5 or the risk-allocation terms in Section 7.

Review Section 3 compensation terms for guaranteed hours, minimum retainer or non-refundable committed spend binding Clear Capital; if present, pair with a convenience-termination exit under Section 6.

Section 6 likely addresses effects of termination but transition assistance and return/deletion of Clear Capital data appear absent; consider adding to Section 6 with a cross-reference to the Section 4 ownership provisions.
